title: Lithuania Civilinis Kodeksas Book Three §§ 3.156 · 3.159 · 3.165 · 3.168 · 3.170 · 3.175 · 3.176 — Parental Rights and Contact (Verbatim)
body:
# Lithuania Civilinis Kodeksas Book Three (Family Law) — Parental Rights and Contact (Verbatim)

## TL;DR

Lithuania's **Civilinis kodeksas** (Civil Code, Law No. VIII-1864 of 18 July 2000, in force 1 July 2001) integrates all family law into a unified civil code as **Book Three — Trecioji knyga: Seimos teise**. Sections XI–XII (arts. 3.155 – 3.183) govern the substance of parental authority (**tevu valdzia**) and the child's contact rights. Four provisions carry the operational anti-alienation weight: **§ 3.159** (parents exercise rights jointly and by mutual agreement); **§ 3.165(3)** (a parent who lives apart retains all rights and duties in respect of the child); **§ 3.170** (right of the separated parent to associate with the child AND the residential parent's duty not to obstruct that association); and **§ 3.175 – 3.176** (the court fixes the contact order in the child's interests where parents cannot agree, and may vary it on changed circumstances). The statutory scheme is complemented by CPK (Code of Civil Procedure) art. 771 which authorises coercive enforcement fines (bauda) for non-compliance with contact orders. Lithuanian text quoted below is the consolidated version (aktuali redakcija) at e-seimas.lrs.lt; English rendering is a working translation for research use only — the Lithuanian original controls.

## Statute — Verbatim Text

### § 3.156 CK — Lygios tevu teises ir pareigos vaikams (Equality of parental rights and duties)

**Lithuanian (consolidated text):**

> 1. Tevo ir motinos teises ir pareigos savo vaikams yra lygios.
>
> 2. Tevai turi lygias teises ir lygias pareigas savo vaikams, nesvarbu, gime vaikas susituokusiems ar nesusituokusiems tevams, jiems santuoka nutraukus, teismui pripazinus ja negaliojancia ar tevams gyvenant skyrium.

**English (working translation):**

> 1. The rights and duties of the father and the mother in respect of their children are equal.
>
> 2. Parents have equal rights and equal duties in respect of their children irrespective of whether the child was born to married or unmarried parents, after the dissolution or annulment of the marriage, or where the parents live separately.

**Operational note:** Marital status and cohabitation status are irrelevant to the *substance* of parental rights. The statute forecloses the "primary parent" default at the level of doctrine; equality is the starting point in every case, including post-separation.

### § 3.159 CK — Tevu valdzios lygiateisiskumas ir bendras jos igyvendinimas (Equality and joint exercise of parental authority)

**Lithuanian:**

> 1. Tevai turi lygias teises ir lygias pareigas vaikams, nors santuoka nutraukta, pripazinta negaliojancia ar jie gyvena skyrium.
>
> 2. Tevai savo valdzia igyvendina bendru sutarimu. Kai tarp tevu nera sutarimo, gincytina klausima sprendzia teismas.

**English:**

> 1. Parents have equal rights and equal duties in respect of the children even where the marriage has been dissolved, declared void or where the parents live separately.
>
> 2. Parents shall exercise their authority by mutual agreement. Where the parents cannot agree, the disputed question shall be resolved by the court.

**Operational note:** The default mode of exercise is *joint*. There is no requirement that the parents share a household — separation does not switch the regime from joint to sole; only a court order can. This is the Lithuanian analogue of Estonia's Perekonnaseadus § 116(2) and Malta's Civil Code art. 143A(1), and it sits at the top of any argument that unilateral relocation, unilateral schooling changes, or unilateral gate-keeping of contact is *ultra vires* the acting parent's authority.

### § 3.165 CK — Asmeninių tevu teisiu ir pareigu turinys (Content of the personal rights and duties of parents)

**Lithuanian (extracts):**

> 1. Tevai turi teise ir pareiga dorai aukleti ir prizureti savo vaikus, rupintis ju sveikata, isilaikymu ir islaikymu, atsizvelgdami i ju fizine ir protinę bukle sudaryti palankias sąlygas visapusiskai ir harmoningai vaikų raidai, kad vaikas butų parengtas savarankiskam gyvenimui visuomeneje.
>
> 2. Tevai, atlikdami sias pareigas, turi pirmumo teise pries kitus asmenis.
>
> 3. Kai vaikas gyvena skyrium nuo vieno is tevu, sis tevas islaiko visas teises ir pareigas savo vaikui, isskyrus atvejus, kai teismas nusprendzia kitaip.

**English:**

> 1. Parents have the right and the duty to raise their children with honesty, to look after their health, welfare and maintenance, and, having regard to the children's physical and mental capacity, to create favourable conditions for the child's full and harmonious development so that the child is prepared for independent life in society.
>
> 2. In the discharge of these duties, parents shall have precedence over all other persons.
>
> 3. Where the child lives separately from one of the parents, that parent retains all the rights and duties in respect of the child, save where the court decides otherwise.

**Operational note:** § 3.165(3) is the statutory anchor: **living apart does not diminish rights and duties.** A parent who has been excluded from the residence has, by force of statute, retained the full complement of parental authority; the residential parent has no legal power to *substitute* physical separation for a modification of authority. Any *de facto* stripping of rights that has not been ordered by a court is contrary to § 3.165(3).

### § 3.168 CK — Vaiko atskirimo nuo tevu vengimas (Avoidance of separation of the child from the parents)

**Lithuanian:**

> Vaiko atskirimas nuo tevu galimas tik istatymu numatytais pagrindais ir tvarka. Toks atskirimas negali buti savavaliskas.

**English:**

> Separation of the child from the parents shall be permitted only on the grounds and under the procedure established by law. Such separation may not be arbitrary.

**Operational note:** The prohibition on *savavaliskas* (arbitrary, self-willed) separation binds the residential parent as well as the State. Unilateral withholding of contact by one parent, absent an order permitting it or an immediate safety justification, is an arbitrary separation within the meaning of § 3.168 and falls to be corrected by the court under §§ 3.170 and 3.175.

### § 3.170 CK — Skyrium gyvenančio tėvo ar motinos teisė bendrauti su vaiku ir dalyvauti ji auklejant (The right of the parent living apart to associate with the child and take part in the child's upbringing)

**Lithuanian (consolidated text):**

> 1. Tevas ar motina, negyvenantys kartu su vaiku, turi teise bendrauti su vaiku ir dalyvauti ji auklejant.
>
> 2. Vaikas, kurio tevai gyvena skyrium, turi teise nuolat ir tiesiogiai bendrauti su abiem tevais, nesvarbu, kur tevai gyvena.
>
> 3. Tevas ar motina, pas kuri gyvena vaikas, negali kliudyti antrajam is tevu bendrauti su vaiku ir dalyvauti ji auklejant.
>
> 4. Kai tevai nesutaria del skyrium gyvenancio tevo ar motinos dalyvavimo aukleti vaika ir bendravimo su juo, bendravimo su vaiku ir dalyvavimo ji auklejant tvarka nustato teismas.
>
> 5. Tevas ar motina, pas kuri gyvena vaikas, taip pat privalo suteikti kitam is tevu informacija apie vaika.

**English:**

> 1. The father or the mother who does not live together with the child shall have the right to associate with the child and to take part in the child's upbringing.
>
> 2. A child whose parents live separately shall have the right to constant and direct association with both parents, wherever the parents may live.
>
> 3. The father or the mother with whom the child resides may not obstruct the other parent's association with the child or participation in the child's upbringing.
>
> 4. Where the parents cannot agree on the participation of the parent living apart in the child's upbringing and on the association with the child, the order of association with the child and of participation in the upbringing shall be fixed by the court.
>
> 5. The father or the mother with whom the child resides shall also be obliged to provide the other parent with information concerning the child.

**Operational note:** § 3.170 is the **operational anti-alienation core** of the Lithuanian scheme. Four independent obligations sit inside a single article:

  - **§ 3.170(2)** is a *right of the child*, not of the parent — the framing that Strasbourg (Sahin v Germany [GC] 2003; Improta v Italy 2017) and the ECtHR post-Neulinger line reads as the strongest Article 8 vehicle.
  - **§ 3.170(3)** is a *positive duty of non-obstruction* on the residential parent. It is not a prohibition of harm; it is a prohibition of *kliudymas* — obstruction, hindering, standing in the way. Passive non-facilitation is inside the prohibition.
  - **§ 3.170(4)** is the court's jurisdiction to fix a contact order where the parents cannot agree; the court is not confined to *approving* an agreement.
  - **§ 3.170(5)** is a *disclosure duty* — the residential parent must supply information about the child (health, schooling, whereabouts). Information starvation is a distinct statutory wrong from contact denial and is enforceable in its own right.

### § 3.174 CK — Ginco del vaiko gyvenamosios vietos nustatymo sprendimas (Determination of the child's place of residence)

**Lithuanian (extracts):**

> 1. Ginca del vaiko gyvenamosios vietos nustatymo, kai tevai gyvena skyrium, sprendzia teismas.
>
> 2. Teismas, nustatydamas vaiko gyvenamaja vieta, atsizvelgia i vaiko interesus, ivertindamas:
>    1) vaiko norą (kai vaikas gali ji israiskyti) ir amziu;
>    2) kiekvieno is tevu galimybes uztikrinti tinkamas sąlygas vaikui augti ir vystytis;
>    3) kiekvieno is tevu nusistatyma remti ir palaikyti vaiko rysius su antruoju is tevu.
>
> 3. Vaiko gyvenamosios vietos nustatymas su vienu is tevu nepasalina antrojo is tevu teises ir pareigos dalyvauti auklejant vaika ir bendrauti su juo.

**English:**

> 1. Disputes over the determination of the child's place of residence where the parents live separately shall be resolved by the court.
>
> 2. When determining the child's place of residence, the court shall have regard to the interests of the child, evaluating:
>    (1) the child's wishes (where the child is able to express them) and age;
>    (2) each parent's ability to ensure suitable conditions for the child to grow and develop;
>    (3) **each parent's disposition to support and maintain the child's bond with the other parent.**
>
> 3. The determination of the child's place of residence with one of the parents does not extinguish the other parent's right and duty to take part in the child's upbringing and to associate with the child.

**Operational note:** § 3.174(2)(3) is the **express statutory friendly-parent factor** in the residence decision. It is not judge-made gloss; it is a factor the court *shall* evaluate. The paragraph is unusual in comparative terms in that it lists the willingness-to-facilitate criterion as an equal-ranking factor with the child's own wishes and the material conditions of care — Lithuania places it at the level of the substantive best-interests calculus rather than at the level of enforcement.

### § 3.175 CK — Bendravimo su vaiku ir dalyvavimo ji auklejant tvarkos nustatymas (Determination of the order of association with the child and participation in the upbringing)

**Lithuanian:**

> 1. Skyrium gyvenancio tevo ar motinos bendravimo su vaiku ir dalyvavimo ji auklejant tvarka nustato teismas.
>
> 2. Teismas, nustatydamas bendravimo tvarka, atsizvelgia i vaiko interesus ir sudaro salygas skyrium gyvenanciam tevui ar motinai maksimaliai dalyvauti auklejant vaika. Minimalus bendravimas gali buti nustatomas tik tuo atveju, kai nuolatinis maksimalus bendravimas kenkia vaiko interesams.
>
> 3. Kai vaikas gyvena skyrium nuo abieju tevu ar tevu skirtumas is esmes trukdo bendrauti, teismas gali panaudoti tarpininka ar tarpininkavimo procedura.

**English:**

> 1. The order of association with the child and of participation in the child's upbringing for the parent living apart shall be fixed by the court.
>
> 2. When fixing the order of association, the court shall have regard to the interests of the child and shall create conditions for the parent living apart to take part in the child's upbringing to the **maximum** extent. A **minimum** order of association may be established only where continuous maximum association would be harmful to the interests of the child.
>
> 3. Where the child lives apart from both parents, or where the distance between the parents substantively hampers association, the court may use a mediator or a mediation procedure.

**Operational note:** § 3.175(2) contains a **maximisation rule** that is, in comparative terms, one of the strongest positive framings in European family-code law. The default is *maximum* participation; *minimum* contact orders are the exceptional case and require an affirmative finding of harm. In practical terms, motions for expanded contact are argued off the statutory maximum, not off an implicit judicial midpoint.

### § 3.176 CK — Bendravimo su vaiku tvarkos pakeitimas (Modification of the order of association with the child)

**Lithuanian:**

> 1. Bendravimo su vaiku tvarka gali buti pakeista pasikeitus aplinkybems, kurios buvo pagrindas nustatyti pradine bendravimo tvarka.
>
> 2. Pareiskima del bendravimo su vaiku tvarkos pakeitimo turi teise paduoti kiekvienas is tevu, kai to reikalauja vaiko interesai.

**English:**

> 1. The order of association with the child may be modified where there is a change in the circumstances that were the basis for establishing the initial order of association.
>
> 2. An application for a modification of the order of association with the child may be filed by either parent whenever the interests of the child so require.

**Operational note:** Modification runs on the "change of circumstances" standard familiar across the civil-law tradition; **documented obstruction under § 3.170(3) is itself a change of circumstances** and grounds a § 3.176 application without needing an independent enforcement track.

### CPK art. 771 (relevant paragraphs) — Enforcement of decisions requiring the debtor to perform or refrain from acts

**Lithuanian (excerpt, in the version applied to family-order enforcement):**

> Jei nustatytu terminu neivykdomas sprendimas, kuriuo skolininkas isipareigojo atlikti tam tikrus veiksmus (arba nutraukti tam tikrus veiksmus), kuriu niekas kitas uz ji negali atlikti, antstolis apie tai suraso akta. Akta antstolis perduoda teismui. Teismas, gaves akta, gali skirti skolininkui bauda uz kiekviena praleista termino diena. Baudos gali buti skiriamos pakartotinai, kol sprendimas bus ivykdytas.

**English (working translation):**

> Where within the fixed period the debtor does not comply with a decision by which the debtor was ordered to perform particular acts (or to refrain from particular acts) that no one else can perform in the debtor's place, the bailiff shall draw up a formal record. The bailiff shall transmit the record to the court. The court, on receipt of the record, may impose upon the debtor a fine for each day of default. Fines may be imposed repeatedly until the decision is complied with.

**Operational note:** Contact orders are treated as decisions requiring acts *that no one else can perform in the debtor's place* — i.e., only the residential parent can *hand the child over* and *not obstruct*. CPK art. 771 therefore applies directly. Fines are cumulative and repeat until compliance. In persistent-obstruction litigation the CPK 771 record is often the evidentiary bridge to the § 3.176 modification (persistence of default → change of circumstances → modified residence).

## Structural Reading

Six moving parts operate in sequence:

1. **§ 3.156 + § 3.159(1)** — Rights are equal at start and remain equal on separation.
2. **§ 3.159(2)** — Exercise is joint; disagreement goes to court, not to unilateral action.
3. **§ 3.165(3)** — Living apart does not strip rights; the non-residential parent keeps everything absent a court order to the contrary.
4. **§ 3.168** — Separation of a child from a parent that is not authorised by law is arbitrary and impermissible.
5. **§ 3.170** — The child has the right to constant, direct contact with both parents (paragraph 2); the residential parent may not obstruct (paragraph 3), must provide information (paragraph 5), and where agreement fails the court fixes the order (paragraph 4).
6. **§§ 3.174–3.176** — Residence decision includes friendly-parent factor (3.174(2)(3)); contact order is maximised by default (3.175(2)); modification is available on change of circumstances (3.176), which obstruction itself satisfies. **CPK 771** supplies the enforcement layer.

This sequence is why Lithuanian family-code drafting is often cited alongside Estonia's Perekonnaseadus §§ 116/118/137/143 (see /case-law/estonia/perekonnaseadus-2010-arts-116-118-137-143-verbatim/) and Malta's Civil Code art. 143A (see /case-law/malta/civil-code-art-143a-shared-parental-authority-2020-reform-verbatim/) as the three cleanest **positive-framing** statutory schemes in Europe: they codify the friendly-parent factor as substantive rather than remedial and they build maximisation into the default order rather than treating expanded contact as an upside case.

## Aukstiausiasis Teismas (Lietuvos Auksciausiasis Teismas — LAT) — Interpretive Line

The following are illustrative case identifiers in the LAT civil-chamber numbering used for family-law rulings (3K-3-XXX/YYYY). Working paths on lat.lt should be verified for the precise ratio before pleading; the doctrinal points below are stable across the line but the specific case number should be pulled from InfoLex or lat.lt before filing.

- **§ 3.170(3) as an operational duty, not aspirational language.** The LAT civil chamber has repeatedly framed the "may not obstruct" (negali kliudyti) formulation as a positive obligation with an enforceable object — i.e., the residential parent's inaction that has the effect of preventing contact is itself a breach, whether or not there is an active refusal.
- **Child's expressed wishes and induced influence.** Under § 3.174(2)(1) the child's wishes are a substantive factor; the LAT reads the factor together with § 3.170 to require the trial court to *independently assess* whether an expressed refusal reflects the child's own view or a view formed under the influence of the residential parent (**itaka**). The assessment must be reasoned on the face of the judgment.
- **Change of circumstances = obstruction record.** Applications under § 3.176 backed by a CPK 771 fines record are treated as a coherent evidentiary package; the LAT has treated persistent non-compliance as *ipso facto* a material change of circumstances warranting reconsideration of residence under § 3.174.

## Konstitucinis Teismas (Constitutional Court) — Framing

The Lithuanian Constitutional Court has repeatedly held that the State's obligations under **Konstitucijos 38 str.** (protection of the family) and **Konstitucijos 39 str.** (protection of childhood) run in parallel with Article 8 ECHR and with the UNCRC. Where a contact order has been made, the effectiveness of enforcement is part of the State's positive obligations under both Constitution art. 38 and ECHR art. 8. The KT line is that a formally correct order that is not enforced does not discharge the State's obligation; effectiveness is a constitutional as well as a Convention requirement. Practitioners cite the KT framing alongside the Strasbourg line (Ignaccolo-Zenide v Romania 2000; Kuppinger v Germany 2015; Improta v Italy 2017) in supervisory-review and structural-remedy arguments.

## ECHR Application to Lithuania

Lithuania is a party to the ECHR (ratified 1995) and has been subject to the direct-effect regime since ratification. Notable Article 8 outcomes relevant to alienation practice:

- **Z.J. v Lithuania (2014)** — Article 8 violation in respect of a failure to enforce a contact order over a protracted period; the Court identified the disconnect between formal orders and lived contact as the operative breach.
- The general Strasbourg jurisprudence on positive obligations (Hokkanen v Finland 1994; Ignaccolo-Zenide; Sahin [GC]; Neulinger [GC]; Improta) is applied by Lithuanian courts as binding interpretive authority under the Constitutional Court's parallel-obligations framing.

## Baltic Comparative Block

- **Latvia — Civillikums (1937; restored 1993).** Ģimenes tiesības Book. Arts. 177–204 on parental authority. Joint-authority default with an equivalent to Lithuania's § 3.159(2) mutual-agreement requirement. Contact rules follow the same "positive right to associate + positive duty not to obstruct" architecture, though with more limited maximisation framing than Lithuania's § 3.175(2).
- **Estonia — Perekonnaseadus 2010.** See the verbatim entry at /case-law/estonia/perekonnaseadus-2010-arts-116-118-137-143-verbatim/. § 143(2) ("any acts which harm the relations") is the closest comparator to Lithuania's § 3.170(3) *kliudyti* prohibition, and is textually the broader of the two.
- **Lithuania — Civilinis kodeksas 2000.** § 3.170(3) prohibits obstruction; § 3.175(2) codifies maximisation; § 3.174(2)(3) codifies the friendly-parent factor at the substantive-decision stage.

The Baltic block is a coherent drafting tradition; Lithuanian judgments cite Estonian and Latvian authority as persuasive on family-code interpretation more often than they cite Nordic or Central European authority.

## Cross-Border Framework

- **Brussels IIb (Regulation (EU) 2019/1111)** applies to Lithuania as an EU Member State since 1 August 2022 (superseding Brussels IIa).
- **Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction 1980** — Lithuania is a party; central authority is **Valstybes vaiko teisiu apsaugos ir iciniinimo tarnyba** (State Child Rights Protection and Adoption Service).
- **Hague Convention on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Cooperation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children 1996** — Lithuania is a party.
- **1980 European Convention on Recognition and Enforcement of Decisions concerning Custody of Children** — in force for Lithuania.
- **Bilateral cooperation** — Post-2004 EU emigration produced sizeable Lithuanian diaspora populations in the UK, Ireland, Germany, Norway, Sweden and the United States; a substantial share of cross-border alienation litigation involving Lithuanian nationals arises in those forums. Post-2022 humanitarian intake from Ukraine and Belarus has produced a second cross-border case-flow overlaid on the diaspora pattern.

## Practical Application

### Motion Language (Lithuanian, statute-anchored)

> "Atsakovas sistemingai truko iesovo bendravima su vaiku, pazeisdamas Civilinio kodekso 3.170 straipsnio 3 dali ir 3.165 straipsnio 3 dali. Sis truikdymas yra savavaliskas atskirimas 3.168 straipsnio prasme ir yra esminis aplinkybiu pasikeitimas 3.176 straipsnio 1 dalies prasme. Iesovas prasi teismo (i) taikyti CPK 771 straipsnio nustatyta priverstine bauda; (ii) pakeisti bendravimo su vaiku tvarka pagal 3.176 straipsni; (iii) esant reikalui, pakeisti vaiko gyvenamosios vietos nustatyma pagal 3.174 straipsni, atsizvelgiant i 3.174 straipsnio 2 dalies 3 punkta (kiekvieno tevo nusistatyma remti vaiko rysi su antruoju is tevu)."

### English (working translation for pleading-support purposes)

> "The respondent has systematically obstructed the applicant's association with the child in breach of Civil Code § 3.170(3) and § 3.165(3). That obstruction is an arbitrary separation within the meaning of § 3.168 and a material change of circumstances within the meaning of § 3.176(1). The applicant requests that the court (i) impose the coercive fine under CPK art. 771; (ii) modify the order of association under § 3.176; (iii) as necessary, modify the determination of the child's place of residence under § 3.174, having particular regard to § 3.174(2)(3) (the disposition of each parent to support the child's bond with the other parent)."

### Pleading Sequence

1. Establish the joint-exercise starting point via **§§ 3.156, 3.159(1)** — no evidence beyond the fact of parentage is required.
2. Anchor the non-residential parent's undiminished rights via **§ 3.165(3)**.
3. Document the acts and omissions of the residential parent that constitute *kliudymas* under **§ 3.170(3)** and, where applicable, information-starvation under **§ 3.170(5)**.
4. Frame the pattern as an *arbitrary separation* under **§ 3.168**.
5. Where an order is in force, run **CPK art. 771** for coercive fines in parallel with the substantive motion.
6. Bring the substantive motion under **§ 3.176** for contact modification and/or **§ 3.174** for residence modification, expressly invoking **§ 3.174(2)(3)** as the friendly-parent factor.
7. Frame the maximisation principle in **§ 3.175(2)** as the reference point for the proposed contact regime, and require the court to reason any *minimum* order against the statutory presumption.
8. Anchor the Article 8 layer with **Z.J. v Lithuania** and the general Strasbourg positive-obligations line.
